lines.text: Jesus tells His disciples about a rich man whose manager is accused of wasting his possessions. The boss calls him in: turn in an account of your management, because you can't be manager any longer. Friend, that is the meeting NOBODY wants on their calendar.
The manager talks it over with himself. Too weak to dig, too ashamed to beg. Then it clicks, and he lands on a plan so that after he's removed, people will welcome him into their homes.

He calls in his master's debtors one by one. The first owes a hundred measures of wine, and the manager says sit down QUICKLY and write fifty. The next owes a hundred measures of wheat, and now it's eighty. Baker, that's the fastest markdown I've ever seen.

wrong_details.true: a hundred measures of olive oil

lines.text: The master commends the dishonest manager because he acted shrewdly. Then Jesus says to use worldly wealth to make friends, so when it's gone, they'll welcome you into eternal dwellings.

Faithful with very little means faithful with much. If you're not faithful with worldly wealth, who'll trust you with ten cities? No servant can serve two masters, and Jesus lands it: "You cannot serve both God and money."
